threads.how: onEnvoyRoleRegained is called only from claimController (after controllerReady succeeds, closure captures token/secret/sessionID; controllerRoleToken deleted) and bootstrapRoot (after the boot's process/ready succeeds; reads capability.secret live). The setup-time registration is gone, so a task subagent's re-bound instance never touches the bridge slot. envoy.ts:90 premise corrected. Regression test: 'a controller's regain hook survives a task subagent's in-process extension re-bind' — second legionExtension(createPi().pi) + subagent-transcript session_start between claim and loss; failed before (controller/ready count 1, 5 s timeout), passes after.

reassertRole fires the hook as `void Promise.resolve().then(() => regained(role, reason)).catch(logger.warn 'envoy: role regain hook failed')` — detached from the heartbeat chain, sync throws covered, never rejects unhandled. Regression test: 'a regain hook that never settles does not block the next heartbeat tick's registration' — hook awaits an unresolved Promise.withResolvers; next tick still POSTs /v1/interests/subscribe; failed before (third registration never lands), passes after.

New `registrationFailed` flag set only when registerSession()/establishSession() rejects, reset on success; afterOutage reads it instead of heartbeatOutageNotified. Test: 'a failed role read does not make the next healthy heartbeat report a regain' (GET /v1/roles returns an unparseable body → warn once; next healthy tick fires no hook); failed before ('reregistered' fired), passes after.

`const id = sessionID` captured at entry beside `topic`; used for the holder comparison, the soft claim, the hand-back unsubscribe and logs; the post-claim guard is `claimedRoleTopic !== topic || sessionID !== id`. No test: the race needs a session rebind between getRole and setRole, which Legion sessions never do; guard-only change.

Both kinds go through rerunReadyAfterRegain → callReadyWithRetry (bounded 5xx/network retries; definitive 4xx propagates to the catch). Catch message now states the consequence: held daemon work stays undelivered until the next regain or boot.
Dropped the 'until now … a human re-ran envoy_role_set' clause from the reassertRole docblock.
Comment now reads: 'The listener no longer names this session: the next tick soft-claims and re-runs controller/ready.'
